query: Accused arrested in an alleged cheating matter without being furnished written grounds of arrest at the time of arrest and remanded to custody in violation of Article 22(1)
reviewNotes: Vihaan Kumar (SC-2025-026) and Mihir Rajesh Shah (SC-2025-027) establish that failure to furnish written grounds of arrest in ordinary IPC/BNS cases invalidates arrest and remand under Article 22(1) and S. 50 CrPC / S. 47 BNSS. Prabir Purkayastha (SC-2024-025) and Pankaj Bansal (SC-2023-024) provide foundational Article 22(1) ratio.

query: Application for regular bail in an offence punishable under 7 years where accused cooperated with investigation and satisfies triple test of not being flight risk
targetAspect: Bail jurisprudence, Section 41A compliance, personal liberty
reviewNotes: Satender Kumar Antil (SC-2022-023) lays down comprehensive bail guidelines for Category A offences (<=7 years) and S. 41A CrPC compliance. Babu Singh (SC-1978-014) establishes foundational 'bail, not jail' constitutional principle under Article 21.

query: Police officer refuses to register First Information Report under Section 154 despite written complaint disclosing cognizable offence
targetAspect: Mandatory FIR registration, cognizable offence, preliminary inquiry
reviewNotes: Constitution Bench in Lalita Kumari (SC-2013-004) mandates that registration of FIR is mandatory under Section 154 of the Code if the information discloses commission of a cognizable offence.

query: Violation of mandatory arrest procedure custodial violence failure to prepare arrest memo and inform family under Article 21 and 22
targetAspect: Custodial safeguards, arrest memo, Article 21 and 22
reviewNotes: D.K. Basu (SC-1996-012) mandates 11 custodial guidelines including arrest memo, inspection memo, relative intimation, and medical examination. Maneka Gandhi (SC-1978-010) establishes fair, just and reasonable procedural due process.

query: Mechanical arrest of husband and relatives under Section 498A IPC without prior notice of appearance under Section 41A CrPC
targetAspect: Matrimonial cruelty, Section 498A pre-arrest scrutiny, Section 41A notice
reviewNotes: Arnesh Kumar (SC-2014-003) prohibits mechanical arrest under S. 498A IPC and mandates S. 41A notice checklist. Satender Kumar Antil (SC-2022-023) reiterates adherence as mandatory for all offences punishable up to 7 years.

query: Quashing of criminal proceedings under Section 482 CrPC where FIR arises purely from civil commercial breach of contract without dishonest intention at inception
targetAspect: Quashing FIR, commercial civil dispute given criminal colour, abuse of process
reviewNotes: State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal (SC-1990-009) sets forth the 7 landmark categories for quashing criminal proceedings under S. 482 CrPC / Art. 226, specifically where commercial breaches lack criminal ingredients.

query: Dishonour of cheque under Section 138 Negotiable Instruments Act drawer signed blank security cheque and claims statutory presumption under Section 139 is rebutted
targetAspect: Section 138/139 NI Act, blank signed cheque, statutory presumption rebuttal
reviewNotes: Bir Singh v. Mukesh Kumar (SC-2019-007) holds that voluntary signing of blank cheque attracts S. 139 presumption of debt. Rangappa v. Sri Mohan (SC-2010-008) settles that reverse burden under S. 139 requires proof on preponderance of probabilities.

query: State surveillance bulk interception of telecommunication metadata and phone tapping infringing fundamental right to privacy under Article 21 and proportionality standard
targetAspect: Right to privacy, metadata surveillance, proportionality review
reviewNotes: Nine-Judge Constitution Bench in K.S. Puttaswamy (SC-2017-001) affirms informational privacy under Article 21 and lays down four-pronged proportionality test for state intrusion. Maneka Gandhi (SC-1978-010) supplies foundational substantive due process.

query: Criminal prosecution for social media post causing annoyance challenged for vagueness overbreadth and chilling effect on freedom of speech under Article 19(1)(a)
targetAspect: Section 66A IT Act, online speech, overbreadth, chilling effect
reviewNotes: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (SC-2015-002) struck down Section 66A of the IT Act for vagueness and unconstitutional chilling effect on Article 19(1)(a) freedom of speech.

query: Reference of commercial dispute to arbitration under Section 8 and Section 11 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act where landlord tenant or arbitrability is contested
targetAspect: Arbitrability four-fold test, Section 8 and Section 11 reference
reviewNotes: Vidya Drolia v. Durga Trading Corp (SC-2020-013) sets out the four-fold non-arbitrability test and rules that landlord-tenant disputes governed by Transfer of Property Act are arbitrable.

query: Challenge to domestic arbitral award under Section 34 of Arbitration Act on grounds of patent illegality and perversity violating public policy of India
targetAspect: Section 34 challenge, patent illegality, public policy of India
reviewNotes: Associate Builders v. DDA (SC-2014-020) defines the boundaries of 'patent illegality' and 'fundamental policy of Indian law' under Section 34, prohibiting reappreciation of evidence.

query: Interim injunction against deceptive similarity well known trademark infringement and dilution in commercial passing off action
targetAspect: Trademark infringement, passing off, well-known mark, deceptive similarity
reviewNotes: Tata Sons Pvt. Ltd. v. Hakunamatata (DEL-2022-016) affirms protection of well-known trademark against deceptive similarity, transborder goodwill dilution, and unauthorized commercial adoption.

query: Constitutional validity of instant triple talaq talaq-e-biddat challenged as manifestly arbitrary and violative of fundamental right to equality under Article 14
targetAspect: Triple talaq, manifest arbitrariness doctrine, Article 14
reviewNotes: Constitution Bench in Shayara Bano v. Union of India (SC-2017-006) set aside Talaq-e-biddat (triple talaq) as manifestly arbitrary and unconstitutional under Article 14.

query: Constitutional challenge to criminalization of consensual adult same-sex relationships under Section 377 IPC violating Article 14 15 and 21
targetAspect: Decriminalization Section 377, constitutional morality, LGBTQ+ rights
reviewNotes: Constitution Bench in Navtej Singh Johar (SC-2018-005) read down Section 377 IPC, holding criminalization of consensual adult same-sex conduct violates Articles 14, 15, 19, and 21.

query: Workplace sexual harassment of women employee guidelines enforcement of fundamental rights under Article 14 19 and 21 in absence of enacted legislation
targetAspect: Workplace sexual harassment, Vishaka guidelines, gender equality
reviewNotes: Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan (SC-1997-011) formulated binding guidelines under Article 32/141 to prevent sexual harassment at workplace, utilizing CEDAW and Articles 14, 19, 21.
